description: Feature inventory for the academic-writer plugin. A checklist for future audits: each top-level feature lists its subfeatures, the source of truth, runtime status, and known issues. status: ok | partial | broken | missing. Regenerate/extend this file whenever features are added or removed.

subfeatures.name: gemini_ocr — single consolidated OCR tool (born-digital text-layer detect via PyMuPDF, sequential Gemini vision batches for scans, response_format concise/detailed enum, page-range + truncation_message, actionable structured errors, Sonnet-only correction left out of scope)
subfeatures.issue: Now wired to a user-facing surface: /academic-writer:ocr command (src/skills/ocr/SKILL.md) resolves a file/directory path, checks the shared GOOGLE_API_KEY credential (env or .academic-helper/secrets.json, same resolution as setup/init), calls gemini_ocr sequentially per document/page batch (following truncation), and writes ocr-output/<name>.ocr.md. The >20MB Files API path is now implemented server-side (gemini-client-ocr-helpers.ts's uploadViaFilesApi(), backed by gemini-client.ts's uploadFileToFilesApi/getFilesApiFile/deleteFilesApiFile): oversized pages are uploaded, polled until ACTIVE (2s interval, 120s timeout), OCR'd via a fileData reference, then deleted (success or failure, try/finally). The skill's per-page-narrowing retry remains as a fallback for when the upload/poll path itself errors (upload failure, FAILED state, or poll timeout).

subfeatures.name: Gemini API key resolution — userConfig (preferred, sensitive-stored) > GOOGLE_API_KEY env > .academic-helper/secrets.json (both casings)
subfeatures.issue: Migrated the plugin's Gemini credential onto Claude Code's userConfig mechanism (manifests/academic-writer.json declares google_api_key, sensitive: true; substituted as USER_CONFIG_GOOGLE_API_KEY in mcpServers.gemini-api.env via ${user_config.google_api_key}). gemini-client.ts's resolveApiKey() checks it first, then falls back to the pre-existing GOOGLE_API_KEY env var, then .academic-helper/secrets.json (GOOGLE_API_KEY or lowercase google_api_key) — all three paths remain fully functional, userConfig is additive/preferred, not a replacement. Investigated whether the 'channels' MCP pattern applied here first (it doesn't — channels is for a server pushing messages into a session, not credential config; userConfig is the actual mechanism, per the Claude Code docs mirror's Plugin manifest reference). scripts/build-plugins.sh now passes userConfig through into the generated plugin.json. Covered by tests/gemini-client-key-resolution.test.ts (9 tests: every precedence pairing plus blank/whitespace optional-field fallthrough).
